stories.title: 📜 2 John
summaryBullets: This letter is from John, the elder. I am writing to the chosen lady and to her children, whom I love in the truth—as does everyone else who knows the truth— (1:1).
because the truth lives in us and will be with us forever. (1:2).
Grace, mercy, and peace, which come from God the Father and from Jesus Christ—the Son of the Father—will continue to be with us who live in truth and love. (1:3).
How happy I was to meet some of your children and find them living according to the truth, just as the Father commanded. (1:4).
I am writing to remind you, dear friends, that we should love one another. This is not a new commandment, but one we have had from the beginning. (1:5).
Love means doing what God has commanded us, and he has commanded us to love one another, just as you heard from the beginning. (1:6).
I say this because many deceivers have gone out into the world. They deny that Jesus Christ came in a real body. Such a person is a deceiver and an antichrist. (1:7).
Watch out that you do not lose what we have worked so hard to achieve. Be diligent so that you receive your full reward. (1:8).
Anyone who wanders away from this teaching has no relationship with God. But anyone who remains in the teaching of Christ has a relationship with both the Father and the Son. (1:9).
If anyone comes to your meeting and does not teach the truth about Christ, don’t invite that person into your home or give any kind of encouragement. (1:10).
Anyone who encourages such people becomes a partner in their evil work. (1:11).
I have much more to say to you, but I don’t want to do it with paper and ink. For I hope to visit you soon and talk with you face to face. Then our joy will be complete. (1:12).
Greetings from the children of your sister, chosen by God. (1:13).
crossRefs: John 14:6 — Jesus is the way, the truth, and the life.
3 John 1:4 — Joy that children walk in the truth.

translationNotes.original: Hebrew: הָאִשָּׁה הַנִּבְחֶרֶת (hāʾiššāh hannibḥéreṯ, sense) — Greek: ἐκλεκτῇ κυρίᾳ (eklektē kyría, NT) — Aramaic: אתתא בחירתא (ʾettatā baḥīrtā)
translationNotes.note: Likely refers to a specific woman believer and her household, though some interpret it figuratively of a church; literally means 'chosen lady.'

stories.keyTakeaway: John greets the elect lady and her children with love in truth, affirming grace, mercy, and peace, and rejoicing in their faithful walk.
